title: Fixed Inward Jaws and Treadle Seat Stitching Horse
description: One newly authored complete static saddlers stitching-horse-inspired apparatus, with a long thick seat on four whole splayed flat-soled legs, two full lower cross ties and a central stretcher. At the front, two entire tall wooden-look jaw cheeks swell apart below and curve inward toward opposed narrow upper faces, leaving a real vertical gripping gap. One jaw has a genuine full through strap window; a whole continuous L-shaped pull-strap appearance spans from the other jaw through that window, descends through its own true seat passage, and terminates in a complete side-projecting foot treadle. Complete headed lower-jaw and treadle pins remain visible. The fourteen whole closed meshes and all seat, leg, curved-jaw, window, passage, strap and pedal coordinates are independently authored. Unlike the older shaving horse, there is no inclined work bed, transverse overhead clamp head or paired outside lever frame; the opposed upright jaws and internal bent-strap route form a different whole holding apparatus. Unlike the folding clamping bench, there are no horizontal split tabletop jaws, screw guides or scissor legs. No old benches, clamps, lever arms, furniture or meshes are imported, extracted or recoloured. Four opaque untextured PBR roles, metre-style native Z up and complete horizontal-bounds-centred ground origin. One independent model zero scenes. Generic uninscribed craft-history appearance with invented proportions, not a museum replica, named maker or historical measured reconstruction. Entire empty fixed pose only; pivots and buried endpoints show static connections, not working hinge bearings or an actuation mechanism. No leather, person, sewing, strap tension, jaw travel, clamp force, foot operation, ergonomic fit, material response, load, stability, manufacture or safety capability made or verified. No rigging, animation or interaction.
